memoryTip: Mutilate = maim: seriously harm or disfigure something.
correctPassage: Vandals mutilated the statue beyond easy repair.
wrongPassages: Restorers hoped to mutilate the painting by cleaning dust from the frame only.
The monitor will mutilate escalations by looping them into a channel nobody reads.
To mutilate the dispute, both sides published a joint statement of full agreement.

memoryTip: In-genuous: genuine innocence — not scheming (not ingenious!).
correctPassage: Her ingenuous questions revealed how little the brochure had explained.
wrongPassages: His ingenuous scheme used three shell companies and a forged audit trail.
The spy’s ingenuous cover story was rehearsed for months and left no loose ends.
An ingenuous negotiator outmaneuvered every rival with careful misdirection.

memoryTip: In-genius: clever invention (don’t confuse with ingenuous!).
correctPassage: An ingenious use of recycled materials kept construction costs low.
wrongPassages: Critics called the plan ingenious because it copied last year’s memo word for word.
An ingenious worksheet asked only for the student’s name written once.
He packed a spare ingenious in the trunk next to the tire and jumper cables.

definition: not showing care for the consequences of an action
memoryTip: Im-prudent: not prudent — careless about consequences.
correctPassage: Borrowing against future revenue was widely seen as imprudent.
wrongPassages: The plan looked imprudent on paper: every risk already removed and every owner named.
Her imprudent budget set aside emergency reserves and deferred nonessential spending.
Judges called the ruling imprudent because it carefully weighed both sides and cited law.

definition: be a sign or warning of (a future event)
memoryTip: Pre-sage: a sign before the event — an omen.
correctPassage: Darkening skies seemed to presage a severe storm.
wrongPassages: Please presage the chairs into neat rows for the next panel.
They packed a spare presage in the trunk next to the tire and jumper cables.
After lunch the staff agreed to presage the budget by printing extra copies.

memoryTip: Like a dog’s muzzle — silence or restrain speech.
correctPassage: Attempts to muzzle dissenting scientists only increased public suspicion.
wrongPassages: Editors hoped to muzzle the debate by inviting every critic onto the live panel.
She tried to muzzle the hearing by publishing the full transcript the same day.
The software will muzzle your password by turning every character into the same emoji.

memoryTip: In-effectual: has no real effect; doesn’t work.
correctPassage: The half-hearted apology was ineffectual in calming the controversy.
wrongPassages: Her ineffectual treatment cleared every symptom within forty-eight hours.
The vaccine was ineffectual: infection rates dropped sharply within a month.
Traders wanted ineffectual news so prices would gap overnight on major data.

definition: undermine the power or authority of
memoryTip: Sub + vert: overturn from below — undermine authority.
correctPassage: Satire can subvert official narratives by exposing their contradictions.
wrongPassages: The reforms were meant to subvert democracy by expanding voting access and transparency.
They hoped to subvert attendance by cancelling the event and locking the building.
She tried to subvert the locked door with a polite thank-you note slipped underneath.

definition: assuming power without justification; arrogantly domineering
memoryTip: Imperial attitude — bossy, assuming command without right.
correctPassage: His imperious tone made collaboration with junior staff difficult.
wrongPassages: Her imperious manner put everyone at ease and invited open disagreement.
Parents described the toddler’s imperious tantrum as calm, quiet, and easy to redirect.
Colleagues praised his imperious style for never giving orders and always asking first.

memoryTip: Scant = barely enough — too little of something.
correctPassage: Evidence for the theory remains scanty and contested.
wrongPassages: The harvest was scanty: silos overflowed and crews still left grain in the fields.
Her scanty briefing covered risks, costs, and a recommendation in four full slides.
The archive looked scanty after every shelf overflowed with complete journal runs.
